sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
Evidence suggests this individual probably was not fully grown.
A sauropod skeleton was found at the Mtuka River, twenty kilometres from Lake Rukwa, in 2004.
The skeleton was excavated between 2005 and 2008.
Mnyamawamtuka was placed in the Titanosauria in 2019.
Mnyamawamtuka lived during the middle Cretaceous, between 110 and 100 million years ago, from the Albian to the Cenomanian, in what is now Africa.
The holotype specimen was found in a layer of the Mtuka Member of the Galula Formation, dating from the Aptian to Cenomanian, very likely between 110 and 100 million years ago.
It is debated whether Mnyamawamtuka belongs outside the Lithostrotia or in a basal position within them as a sister species of Malawisaurus.
